facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected in 1923 during an expedition led by J. B. Abbott.
facts.quote: The holotype of Secernosaurus koeneri was collected in 1923 as part of an expedition by the Field Museum led by J. B. Abbott.

facts.statement: The genus was formally named by Brett-Surman in 1979.
facts.quote: In 1979, Brett-Surman named Secernosaurus.

facts.statement: Secernosaurus koerneri was the first formally named hadrosaurid species from South America.
facts.quote: Secernosaurus koeneri was the first species of South American hadrosaurid to be formally named.

facts.statement: The name Secernosaurus means "separated reptile," referring to its geographic separation from Laurasian hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The genus name Secernosaurus means "separated reptile" and comes from the Latin verb sēcernō, meaning to sever or divide, in reference to its geographic location separated from Laurasian hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: The species name koerneri honors the paleontologist Harold E. Koerner.
facts.quote: The species name S. koerneri honors Harold E. Koerner.

facts.statement: The type specimen measures approximately 4 to 5 meters in length and may represent a mature individual rather than a subadult.
facts.quote: The type specimen pertains to an individual approximately 4 - 5 m long, which was initially suggested to be a subadult, but has been suggested that it may have been more mature than previously thought.

facts.statement: The neuroanatomy of Secernosaurus koerneri is very similar to that of Northern Hemisphere hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: The neuroanatomy of S. koerneri was very similar to that of hadrosaurids from the Northern Hemisphere.

facts.statement: Secernosaurus lived in South America, a region distinct from the Laurasian continents where most other hadrosaurids lived.
facts.quote: This genus and its close relatives lived in South America, unlike most hadrosaurids, which lived in the Laurasian continents of Eurasia and North America.

facts.statement: Secernosaurus fossils are found in the uppermost part of the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation.
facts.quote: It is from this uppermost part of the formation that Secernosaurus is from.

facts.statement: Palynological data suggest the climate in the upper deposits of the formation was mild with balanced wet and dry seasons during the end of the Cretaceous and Paleocene.
facts.quote: However, palynological data indicate that during the upper deposits of the formation at the very end of the Cretaceous and into the Danian age of the Paleocene, the climate became milder once again and returned to a balanced wet and dry season.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Secernosaurus arrived in South America via a dispersal event from North America during the Campanian, possibly using the proto-Antilles island chain.
facts.quote: Their presence in South America is likely to represent a dispersal event from North America during the Campanian, when the proto-Antilles may have formed an island chain that allowed land vertebrates to cross between the two continents.

facts.statement: Secernosaurus koerneri lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Secernosaurus koerneri es la única especie conocida del género extinto Secernosaurus ("reptil aislado") de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Initial analysis of the holotype suggested Secernosaurus was a small duck-billed dinosaur about 3 meters long, 1.2 meters high, and weighing between 200 and 400 kilograms.
facts.quote: Los restos descubiertos inicialmente de Secernosaurus, el espécimen holotipo FMNH PR 13423, indicaron que es un dinosaurio de pico de pato de pequeño tamaño, de apenas 3 metros de largo, 1,2 de alto y entre 200 y 400 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Fossils of Secernosaurus have been found in the Lago Colhué Huapi and Los Alamitos formations.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han encontrado además en las formaciones Lago Colhué Huapi y Los Alamitos.

facts.statement: Recent evidence in 2022 suggests that Secernosaurus koerneri, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, and "Kritosaurus" australis are valid taxa.
facts.quote: En 2022 nueva evidencia nos permite reconocer que Secernosaurus koerneri, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis y "Kritosaurus" australis son taxones válidos.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses classify Secernosaurus within the hadrosaurid tribe Kritosaurini and subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses have found Secernosaurus to be a member of the hadrosaurid tribe Kritosaurini within the subfamily Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: Secernosaurus is distinguished by a subhorizontal crest on the ilium separating the preacetabular notch from the pubic pedicle, a longitudinal crest on the dorsal surface of the postacetabular process, and a twisted distal end of that process.
